analysis.title: Europe Hits Panic Mode — Smart Money Buys The Small-Cap Carnage
key_insights: SX5E printed two bearish candles in a row and is testing the 6200 area in futures, which the note calls make-or-break. The long-term trend line sits near the same level and the index is breaking below its 100-day moving average. The 200-day is much further down.
The note ties the SX5E weakness to French spreads. Overlaying the index on the OAT/Bund spread shows the dynamic, though the note says more than France is driving the index.
V2X is spiking, but the rise in iTraxx Main is much larger. Credit stress is moving ahead of European equity vol.
The euro is the most oversold since 2015. The French rate move has spread to Italian yields, which are also seeing large moves.

TS Lombard argues Europe may be more exposed than the US at the margin to Japanese repatriation. French bonds are Japan's second-largest foreign bond holding after USTs and its largest single European sovereign exposure.

JGB yields now exceed yields on hedged DM government bonds and the long end has become relatively more stable, which removes a reason for Japanese institutions to stay abroad. Lombard expects a more active BoJ, with a December hike as base case and October still live.

US banks have sold off sharply while European banks have barely moved. BofA raises the possibility that EZ banks are late rather than US banks being the anomaly, since European curves are flattening, growth expectations are deteriorating and SX7E remains one of the year's top performers.

BofA finds SX7E downside screens better than several other cross-asset tail hedges when current hedge cost is compared with historical drawdowns. Elevated bank put skew makes put spreads relatively attractive. The Dec-26 30D-20D put spread offers more than 4x maximum payout.

GS's Robert Quinn reports non-dealers bought about $3bn of Russell 2000 futures between Sept 1 and 22, with asset managers at $2.2bn. Non-dealer positioning entered September at a multi-year low. The open question is whether this contrarian buying reverses the move or gets overwhelmed by credit deterioration.

sector_views.rationale: BofA says the gap with US banks may close from the European side, since EZ banks could be late. It sees SX7E downside protection as reasonably priced.
Non-dealers have been buying Russell 2000 futures after the rates-driven selloff. GS leaves open whether this is the start of a reversal or whether credit deterioration overwhelms it.

macro_indicators.reading: Hike in December as base case, October still live
macro_indicators.interpretation: TS Lombard expects a more active BoJ. Higher JGB yields could prompt Japanese repatriation from foreign bonds, including French sovereigns.

trade_ideas.description: Buy SX7E Dec-26 30D-20D put spread as a hedge on European banks
trade_ideas.rationale: Bank put skew is elevated, which makes put spreads relatively cheap, and the downside screens well against historical drawdowns.

risk_factors: French spread widening could break the SX5E 6200 level and its long-term trend line.
Credit stress, shown by iTraxx Main, is wider than equity vol implies.
Rising Japanese yields could trigger repatriation out of European sovereign bonds, with France the largest exposure.
A rates problem could become a growth problem for European banks.
Credit deterioration could overwhelm the contrarian buying in Russell 2000 futures.
vol_and_positioning: V2X is spiking, but iTraxx Main is moving much more.
BofA: bank put skew is elevated versus the rest of Europe, which makes put spreads relatively attractive. The Dec-26 30D-20D SX7E put spread offers more than 4x maximum payout.

GS: non-dealers bought about $3bn of Russell 2000 futures between Sept 1 and 22, $2.2bn of it from asset managers, with smaller amounts from hedge funds and non-reportables. Non-dealer positioning started September at a multi-year low.
geopolitical: French political and fiscal stress is pressuring OAT spreads versus Bunds and spreading to Italian yields.
cross_bank_references: BofA's work raises the opposite possibility: what if EZ banks are simply late?
Goldman's Robert Quinn notes that non-dealers bought around $3bn of Russell 2k futures
